data.name: Githika
data.gender_notes: Githika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Githa refers to a collection of verses or a song. This name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'git', meaning song or melody. In Hindu mythology, Gita is also the name of the sacred text, the Bhagavad Gita, which is a conversation between Lord Krishna and Arjuna. The name Githika carries the meaning “Song, Melody” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Githika usually hope their child will grow to embody song, melody and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the divine essence of music and spiritual wisdom.
data.etymology: Githika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Song, Melody.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Githika total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Githa has a rich cultural significance in Indian history, especially in the context of the epic Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita. In the narrative, Gita represents the divine teachings of Lord Krishna, who shared his wisdom on various aspects of life, philosophy, and spirituality to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. This name is a reminder of the importance of knowledge, wisdom, and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Githa denotes a deep connection with the divine. Its meaning "song" symbolizes the inner voice that guides us on our spiritual journey. The name also reminds one of the Bhagavad Gita's teachings on selflessness, non-attachment, and devotion to God. By embracing the name Githa, one can strive to experience a deeper connection to the divine and seek enlightenment through the wisdom found in the sacred scriptures.
